turns.content: hey julian mentioned something about new members needing an email invite before voting but the charter just says five weekend sessions in eight weeks. i have my dates jotted down - june 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th. does the written rule mean i qualify or does his comment override it? also fwiw showing up five weekends in a row was kind of a big deal for me socially so i'd like to know for sure 🤔

Based on the wording you quoted, **five qualifying weekend sessions within eight weeks would satisfy the written attendance requirement**. Your listed dates are five sessions within 29 days, assuming each was an official weekend session.

Julian’s comment would override that only if the email-invite requirement appears in a controlling rule—such as a valid charter amendment, bylaws, or an adopted voting procedure—or if the charter expressly authorizes someone to impose that condition. An informal comment alone does not change the written rule.

To confirm, ask for the governing text and a record of any amendment:

> I attended official weekend sessions on June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29, which appears to meet the charter’s requirement of five weekend sessions within eight weeks. Julian mentioned that new members also need an email invitation before voting. Could you point me to the current written provision or adopted amendment establishing that additional requirement and confirm my voting eligibility?

My recommendation: rely provisionally on the charter, but obtain written confirmation before the vote.

ok so that's what i thought but julian's comment had me second-guessing myself. thanks for the sanity check.

the charter text is literally just one page, no amendments or anything. so the written rule should stand, right?

Yes. **If the charter is the controlling document, contains the complete eligibility rule, and no valid amendment or separately authorized rule exists, its written requirement governs.** Julian’s comment alone does not add an email-invitation condition.

On the facts you reported, five official sessions on June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 fall within eight weeks, so you meet the stated attendance requirement. Retain your attendance record and request written confirmation of eligibility before voting.

yeah that makes sense. one page, no amendments, i can work with that.

so i'm thinking i should just show up to the next casual saturday session and mention it to julian myself. like "hey i checked the charter and i think i'm active now"

That wording accurately presents it as your reading rather than overstating a formal determination:

> “Hey Julian, I checked the charter. I attended the five Saturday sessions on June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29, all within eight weeks, so I believe I now meet the active-member requirement. Can you confirm?”

Bring or save a copy of the charter and your attendance dates. If he still cites an email invitation, ask him to identify the written rule or adopted decision that requires it.

yeah that sounds like a sensible way to bring it up. not too pushy but still clear.\n\none thing though — he's been running the club for years and everyone kind of defers to how he does things. do you think he'll just go along with the charter text or is this the kind of thing where unwritten custom usually wins out in practice? 🤷

It is not possible to predict Julian’s response from his tenure or others’ deference. Those facts suggest he may have **practical influence**, but they do not establish authority to add eligibility conditions.

An unwritten custom can prevail **in practice** if members routinely accept it, but it does not ordinarily override a controlling charter unless the charter authorizes such procedures or the organization has formally adopted the custom through another valid mechanism.

Use the wording above. If Julian invokes custom, ask:

> “Has the email-invitation requirement been formally adopted or recorded anywhere? If not, can we follow the charter for this vote and put any proposed change through the charter’s amendment process?”

My recommendation: seek a written eligibility confirmation before relying on either Julian’s personal interpretation or the club’s informal practice.

yeah that all makes sense. i guess i'll just see how it goes on saturday.

it'd be nice if the charter is what actually counts, you know? because then the effort i put in actually means something official, not just a vibe check from julian.

Under the facts you reported, the charter’s five-session requirement is the only documented eligibility standard, and your five listed sessions satisfy it if they were official sessions. That gives you a specific basis for claiming active-member status; Julian’s unwritten email condition has not been established as governing.

On Saturday, keep the discussion factual:

> “I attended the five qualifying sessions listed in the charter, so I understand that I’m now an active member. Is there any formally adopted rule that changes that?”

If he cannot identify one but denies your status, ask for the decision and its basis in writing.
